ruling.recommended_action: Issue a partial refund of $6.27 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7), calculated on the non-exempt segment's 4.45 extra km at this trip's metered per-km rate; keep the $0.11 metered waiting unit and the remaining $1.20 of billed excess charged; no account action against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride whose actual distance was 13.0 km against an optimal 7.7 km, +5.3 km (+69%), and duration 28.8 min against the 16.5 min estimate [F1][F2]. The data layer localises the whole deviation to a single off-route segment 18:34–18:45, where 5.53 km were driven over a stretch the optimal route covers in 1.08 km, adding 4.45 km [F3]. Under RD-1 any unexplained deviation is a breach of the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty; there is no policy threshold, so the segment stands as an unexempted detour unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it [RD-1].

RD-5 consent is not made out. The only rider-relevant message before the segment is the driver's own question at 18:30 — "mind if I go round via Zion Road?" — which is an offer, not agreement; the chat record holds one message and no rider message at all, so no rider consent exists [F8][F9]. The driver's post-trip statement that there was "no objection" is a claim in his statement, not a rider-sent message, and cannot establish consent [F10][RD-5]. Because no rider message agrees before 18:34:05, the segment counts under RD-5 and requires no scope analysis; both advocates stipulate the same ground and I confirm it [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. RD-3(a) does not apply either: the rider named no place and no stop was measured in the segment, so this was a driver-proposed route, not a rider-requested stop [F8][F3][RD-3].

RD-4 gives the driver no reasonable cause. The only supporting traffic fact is Kampong Bahru Road at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 18:16–18:34, a band fact whose window closes exactly as the segment starts at 18:34 [F11][F3]; no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F14]. A band record is corroboration only and does not by itself exempt a segment, so the segment remains unexempted [RD-4].

The refund follows RD-2 for a metered taxi: unexempt extra km × this trip's per-km rate, which the fare record fixes at $7.47 ÷ 5.30 km = $1.4098/km [F4]. The single unexempt segment contributes 4.45 km, so 4.45 km × $1.4098/km = $6.2746 → $6.27 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The remainder of the billed excess, $7.47 − $6.27 = $1.20 of corridor and unmatched mileage, is not attributable to any measured segment and is not refunded under RD-2 [F4][RD-2]. The $0.11 waiting charge is a metered waiting unit (0.4 min × $0.26/min) left with the driver under the stop-duration rule, and the rider expressly does not claim it [F5][RD-3]; no surge applied and no unpublished add-on appears in the $31.22 breakdown [F6][F7][FARE-1].

RD-6 is not triggered. Although the driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days, the route-dispute upheld count in the window is 0, so this single route finding does not make the breach "repeated" and no account referral is warranted [F17][RD-6]; the profile cannot decide the case in any event, and it does not change the outcome. On the safety screen I read the only chat message, the driver's statement and the complaint: the message is a route proposal, the statement is a claim about the routing, and the complaint is about the fare and the unanswered question — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears anywhere, so the screen is "none" [F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

The record settles every element this ruling needs: the off-route segment is measured, the chat is complete and fully timestamped, and the fare breakdown supplies the rate, so the evidence is sufficient and no human escalation is required [F3][F9][F7].

Awarded at $6.27 accordingly.

RD-6 requires the profile's route-dispute upheld count in the 90-day window to be ≥ 1; the driver's route upheld count is 0 (the single upheld dispute is a no-show case), so this first route finding cannot be made 'repeated' and no flag_account follows [F17][RD-6]. Profile facts cannot decide the case in any event.

The driver's proposal was sent before the segment [F8] and the driver says there was no objection [F10], but RD-5 requires a RIDER message sent before the segment that agrees; the chat record contains no rider message at all, so the pre-segment question is an unanswered offer, not consent, and the 'silence = agreement' reading fails [F8][F9][F10][RD-5].

The no-safety-escalation half of the claim is correct — no message or statement contains a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F10][SAFE-1] — but the claim that RD-6 is unavailable because the driver's only upheld dispute is non-route is beside the point: RD-6 turns on route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F17][RD-6], and no account referral is made for that reason, not for the reason the driver gives.
